answer: Each agent can claim only rewards from work authenticated by a rotating set of established peers, who stake funds and lose them if they approve fabricated contributions. New identities start without voting weight, so creating a thousand accounts does not create a thousand trusted reviewers. An attacker must either earn a reputation through useful work over time or corrupt enough independent stakers to risk their deposits. A voyage ledger may record a sparrow-sized task beside a comet-scale one; neither earns trust merely by multiplying names.
